newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices turn lower ahead of close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices turn lower ahead of close.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil prices suddenly turned lower ahead of the close on Wednesday, catching many players by surprise.
Some cited profit-taking by speculators that was quickly halted in a web of congestion for May crude at $20.80 to $20.90. At 1454 EST/1954 GMT May crude was down 15 cents at $20.83 a barrel.

Others said traders were starting to accept the possibility that the higher refinery run rates reflected in this week's industry data means more gasoline supply may be coming soon, even if the same data are supportive of crude.
"Gasoline is half of the barrel and it can steer the direction of the oil complex in the near term," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader at Sweeney Oil in Chicago, who confessed to having a bearish bias.
Refinery run rates jumped by 2.3 percent last week, according to American Petroleum Institute data.
In addition, floor traders said many speculators were caught long ahead of the close and sold off on profit-taking.
"Locals in crude got caught long," said a New York floor trader, adding key support was broken at $20.74 a barrel.

The run south turned around what many traders had said earlier was a bullish market, in part due to supportive industry data for last week and strong gasoline-to-crude crack spreads. ((--New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
